bull_case: VKTX is spiking pre-market on a strong GLP-1 trial result with 22% weight loss, which could lift the broader obesity drug space. MLKN posted a clean beat even stripping out tariff refunds, and order trends rose 3.5% year-over-year. CGNX's acquisition of RealSense signals confidence in Physical AI and robotics demand, a growth theme that could re-rate the stock.
bear_case: AZO's beat was heavily driven by tariff refunds and non-cash LIFO impacts, masking weak domestic comps of plus 1.6% versus expectations of plus 3.1%. THO missed on earnings and gross margins, with management citing stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation straining consumer budgets. THO's cautious tone on the macro consumer backdrop could weigh on other discretionary and durable goods names.

company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — tariff refunds added 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO impact added another 105 basis points. Domestic comps grew only 1.6% versus expectations of 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened by 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final eight weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex deeper into the high-growth robotics and Physical AI supply chain.

MillerKnoll reported fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat holds up even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — adjusted EPS would have been 42 cents, still ahead of consensus. Sales declined 3.3% organically to $923.4 million, missing the $943.2 million estimate, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed modestly while EPS guidance was maintained, and fiscal Q2 EPS guidance is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The leadership change is a modest operational update with no financial guidance revision attached.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% — well below the 13.85% expected — despite revenue coming in slightly above estimates at $2.311 billion. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, inflation, and rising material costs as meaningful headwinds throughout the selling season. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog year-over-year.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The result is a meaningful data point in the competitive obesity drug space and validates VK2735 as a credible contender. This is a significant positive catalyst that could re-rate the stock and lift sentiment across the GLP-1 sector.

sectors: RV and consumer durables face headwinds per THO commentary — stubborn rates, fuel costs, and inflation are pressuring household budgets. The GLP-1 and obesity drug space gets a positive signal from VKTX's VK2735 data. Robotics and Physical AI theme is reinforced by CGNX's RealSense acquisition. Auto parts retail shows soft underlying demand trends beneath AZO's headline beat.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, covering six names reporting before the open. There is no broad macro or index commentary in this note, so let's go straight to the tape.

Viking Therapeutics is the headline mover — shares are spiking in pre-market after the company reported positive results for its GLP-1 weight loss drug, with trial participants showing 22% weight loss. That is a big number, and it puts Viking firmly on the map as a serious competitor in the obesity drug space. Expect this to move the broader GLP-1 sector at the open.

On AutoZone — the headline beat looks good, EPS of $56.05 versus $54.03 expected, but peel back the layers and the quality is poor. Tariff refunds contributed 145 basis points to gross margins, a non-cash LIFO adjustment added another 105 basis points, domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus the plus 3.1% the Street wanted, and operating expenses worsened year-over-year. Management did say sales improved in the back half of the quarter, but this is not a clean beat.

MillerKnoll is a cleaner story. They earned 53 cents against a 36-cent estimate, and here is the key point — even stripping out an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, adjusted EPS was 42 cents, still well ahead of consensus. Orders grew 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year EPS guidance was held steady. That is a real beat.

THOR Industries missed. EPS came in at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the nearly 14% the Street modeled. Management's language was cautious — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, inflation squeezing household budgets. The order backlog in North American towable RVs did surge roughly 75% year-over-year, which is a genuine bright spot, and management is taking structural cost actions. But the near-term read is soft, and the macro commentary here is a warning sign for consumer discretionary broadly.

Cognex announced it is acquiring RealSense, the depth-sensing camera leader for robotics and Physical AI, for roughly $500 million upfront. RealSense is growing revenues more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic bet on the Physical AI buildout theme.

Pentair named a new CFO effective November 1st — a housekeeping item, no guidance change attached.

Bottom line for today: VKTX is the momentum name, MLKN is the clean beat, THO is the cautionary consumer read, and AZO's beat needs a quality asterisk. Stay selective.
